title: GRACE: A Language Model Framework for Explainable Inverse Reinforcement Learning

mechanism.domainTask: Recovering interpretable executable reward functions from expert and negative trajectories for inverse reinforcement learning
mechanism.populationDetail: The initial reward functions form a flat population R; no island or tree organization is reported.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive is described; the bounded reward population itself retains the top-P candidates.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Each iteration takes the top P reward functions from the union of the current population and newly mutated candidates.
mechanism.generationDetail: The first reward population is generated from scratch from demonstrations; later candidates broadly modify one selected reward program using its code and failure examples.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Sampled low-fitness states and the reward values assigned to them are embedded into the next mutation prompt; optional debug output can add state-level diagnostics.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The single parent reward is sampled proportional to exp(fitness); low-fitness states are separately sampled as debugging context, not as parents.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A reward population is improved through an outer active data-collection loop: PPO trained on the current best reward generates trajectories that are added as negative examples for subsequent reward refinement.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/GRACE A Language Model Framework for Explainable Inverse Reinforcement Learning.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Survey already cites GRACE under application and parent selection. Add mechanism coverage for flat population, top-P replacement, initialization/mutation prompts, model usage, evaluator metadata, and implicit exploration/exploitation. The optional goal-cleaning/debug prompts are auxiliary and should not be confused with separate evolutionary operators.
